This is incorrect. In fact only a tiny fraction of all money is actually created by the government - around 3% in fact.

The rest is created by private banks. How? Fractional reserve lending. Fractional reserve is far more insidious than it seems at first. What a fractional reserve means is that banks only need to hold a fraction of what they lend out - 10% in most countries including the US. So how does this create money?

  • I go deposit $100 at Bank America.
  • They now lend out $90 and keep $10 on hand. If I wanted my $100 back, they wouldn't have it. This is legal and where the central bank would come save the day.
  • That $90 gets spent and deposited at another bank, if not the same one. This bank now keeps $9 on hand and lends out $81.
  • This process continues onward until there's no money left.

In the end my real money deposit of $100 will end up creating $1000 of new money that's created in the form of debt. This is how nearly all new money is created. The government themselves print only a tiny fraction of all new money that enters into the system. This is also a very dangerous game as most of all new money being created in the form of debt has enormous implications, but let's keep it simple for now!
